title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice.
authors: Justina Zemaite; Stefan Erler; Ulrich Schafer; Steffen Vormfelde; Bjoern Andrew Remppis; Katja Bohmann; Barbara Maria Januszewski; Christof Burgdorf
abstract:
Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice.
Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80-86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73-84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria.
The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6-25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5-5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36-54) mm Hg and 72 (60-87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5-9) mm Hg and 12 (9-15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27-43) mm Hg and 59 (44-70) mm Hg to 9 (7-11) mm Hg and 16 (14-23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively.
TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

title: Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
authors: Toshiharu Sassa; Megumi Maeda; Futoshi Oda; Tomohiro Sakamoto; Haruhisa Fukuda
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk.
This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107).
Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67).
Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

title: Perioperative Care of Heart Failure, Arrhythmias, and Valvular Heart Disease.
authors: Avital Y O'Glasser; Efrén C Manjarrez
abstract: Frequently, the question of whether or not a patient is stable for surgery boils down to the question, "Does this patient need a preoperative stress test?" However, coronary artery disease and ischemic heart disease are only some of the many cardiac conditions that patients present with preoperatively-and that can negatively impact their intraoperative management and postoperative outcomes. This article will explore the evidence based, patient centered best practices surrounding the perioperative evaluation and management of heart failure, arrhythmias, and valvular heart disease.

title: Cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1 is a novel prognostic biomarker in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Yu Zhang; Fangfang Wan; Chen Li; Bo Wang; Mo Zhang; Minjie Lu; Lianming Kang; Liwen Liu; Jizheng Wang; Lei Song
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibits great prognostic heterogeneity, necessitating the identification of high-risk patients for timely treatment. This study aimed to find novel prognostic biomarkers directly from diseased cardiac tissue to improve risk stratification of HCM. We utilized a myocardial transcriptome discovery cohort (n = 246; median follow-up 6.8 years) alongside two independent plasma validation cohorts (Beijing, n = 1,238; follow-up 2.5 years; Xi'an, n = 402; follow-up 4.8 years). The primary and secondary endpoints were cardiovascular death and sudden cardiac death (SCD), respectively. In the discovery cohort, myocardial expression of CECR1 (cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1, also known as ADA2, Adenosine Deaminase 2) demonstrated the strongest association with cardiovascular death (P = 9.6 × 10-5). Plasma CECR1 levels correlated modestly but significantly with myocardial expression. In the Beijing validation cohort, decreased plasma CECR1 predicted increased risks of cardiovascular death (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 3.731, P < 0.001) and SCD (adjusted HR 7.398, P < 0.001), with areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.720 and 0.798, respectively. These findings were replicated in the Xi'an validation cohort. Integrating plasma CECR1 into the HCM Risk-SCD model significantly enhanced its predictive performance, increasing the AUC from 0.723 to 0.845 (P = 0.031) in the Beijing validation cohort and consistently improving it from 0.600 to 0.781 (P = 0.018) in the Xi'an validation cohort. In conclusion, CECR1 represents a novel prognostic biomarker of HCM. Measurement of CECR1 may improve risk stratification by facilitating the identification of individuals at higher risk of cardiovascular mortality. CECR1 assessment may provide additional information for SCD risk evaluation and support clinical decision-making regarding implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy.

title: Histologically Confirmed Myxedematous Myocardial Involvement in Severe Hypothyroidism With Concomitant Bicuspid Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Shubhang Sharma-Sharma; Jaime Galindo-Uribe; Sebastián Gutiérrez-Alanís; Aldo César Cázares-Diazleal; Zuilma Yurith Vásquez-Ortiz; Sandra Graciela Rosales-Uvera; Bernardo Pérez-Enríquez; Braulio Martínez-Benítez
abstract:
Histologically confirmed myxedematous myocardial involvement is rare and may be difficult to recognize when another cause of ventricular hypertrophy and fibrosis coexists.
A 40-year-old man with longstanding, inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism presented with exertional dyspnea and a large goiter. Echocardiography showed severe bicuspid aortic stenosis, moderate aortic regurgitation, marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrated extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving approximately 26% of myocardial mass. After thyroid optimization, he underwent aortic valve replacement. Myocardial biopsy showed severe cardiomyocyte atrophy, interstitial mucin deposition, and extensive replacement fibrosis; Congo red staining was negative.
Severe aortic stenosis provided an alternative explanation for the myocardial phenotype, and multimodality imaging alone could not distinguish pressure-overload remodeling from hypothyroidism-related myocardial injury.
Histopathology established concomitant myxedematous myocardial involvement, highlighting the diagnostic value of tissue characterization in severe hypothyroidism.

title: Same-Day Discharge After Percutaneous Transaxillary Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using Self-Expanding Valve.
authors: Paraskevi Trivilou; Debbie Stewart; John Reicher; Richard Edwards; Mohammad Alkhalil
abstract:
The safety of same-day discharge (SDD) following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established strategy in patients undergoing the transfemoral approach. The feasibility of SDD in patients undergoing transaxillary TAVI has not been reported.
We present a 76-year-old male patient who underwent successful elective transaxillary TAVI. He had severe aortic stenosis, normal left ventricular function, and a background of diabetes, chronic liver disease, and right above-knee amputation. The access site was managed with 2 ProGlide devices with excellent hemostasis. There were no significant electrocardiogram changes postprocedure. Comprehensive postdischarge surveillance was provided, including a welfare telephone call on the following day.
To our knowledge, this is the first case in the literature of SDD following transaxillary TAVI. Such a strategy requires appropriate patient selection, meticulous procedural planning, rigorous postdischarge monitoring strategy, and can only be considered in highly selected cases.

title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
authors: Suzanne J Baron; Benjamin Z Galper; Marcella A Kelley; Soumya G Chikermane; Shannon M E Murphy
abstract:
Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown.
Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR.
3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804).
In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

title: IVUS-Guided Dobutamine Challenge to Guide Anomalous RCA PCI: An Interesting Case Report.
authors: Stefanos Votsis; Mehmet Cilingiroglu; Cezar Iliescu; Konstantinos Dean Boudoulas; Konstantinos Marmagkiolis
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: Congenital coronary artery anomalies are quite uncommon-they are observed in 1.3% of the coronary angiograms. Although most of them are benign, some coronary anomalies are associated with poor clinical outcomes. The exact mechanism of these outcomes in patients with anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with interarterial course is hypothesized to be either compression of the coronary artery during its course between the aorta and the pulmonary artery, or obstruction of the coronary flow during exercise due to the acute angulation of the RCA ostium. We present the case of a 54 y/o patient with NSTEMI, who, after a diagnostic coronary angiogram and coronary CT, was found to have complex coronary artery disease, including an anomalous RCA from the left aortic cusp with "malignant" interarterial course. In order to determine the optimal treatment, we proceeded with IVUS assessment of the ostial and proximal RCA with dobutamine challenge, which showed significant stenosis of both the RCA ostium and the interarterial segment at the peak dose of the dobutamine challenge. As a result a decision was made to treat both the RCA ostium and its interarterial segment with PCI, producing an excellent final result. Our case underscores the importance of the combination of IVUS and dobutamine challenge in order to answer the ever-important pathophysiologic mechanism of a lesion and accordingly provide tailor-made treatment for anomalous coronary arteries.

title: One-stop photon-counting CT angiography for simultaneous assessment of cardio-cerebrovascular lesions: A case report.
authors: Yuanyuan Wan; Dandan Zou; Jinhui Lan; Fan Yang; Jizhao Jiang; Yongwei Liu; Wei Tian; Gang Wang; Yanli Zhang
abstract: We report a 73-year-old male admitted for 2-year progressive dysuria, with incidental detection of abnormal cardiovascular signs on physical examination. Initial evaluation via energy-integrating detector computed tomography (EID-CT) coronary angiography and cranial magnetic resonance imaging identified key vascular abnormalities, while subsequent photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) combined cardio-cerebral computed tomography angiography (CTA) provided more detailed assessment of stenosis severity, plaque composition, and the entire vascular bed. The combined PCD-CT scan delineated synchronous lesions in detail: proximal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery plaque, ascending aortic dilatation with left coronary sinus aneurysm compressing the left atrium, and occlusion of the intracranial right vertebral artery. Importantly, PCD-CT cardio-cerebral CTA yielded a lower radiation dose compared with standalone EID-CT coronary angiography. With spectral reconstruction, the severity of LAD stenosis was re-evaluated and interpreted as mild stenosis, a lower grade than that assessed by EID-CT; meanwhile, 0.4 mm thin-slice imaging enabled detailed compositional analysis of the coronary plaque, with imaging features suggestive of a stable plaque. Based on multidisciplinary discussion integrating all imaging findings and clinical context, a treatment strategy was formulated: prioritize high-risk aortic lesion management, synchronously perform coronary artery bypass grafting for myocardial ischemia prevention, and electively address intracranial stenosis. This case demonstrates the preliminary clinical value of PCD-CT as a supportive imaging modality for the evaluation and multidisciplinary management of concurrent cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.

title: Progression rates of aortic stenosis in patients with calcific and rheumatic heart disease in Saudi Arabia.
authors: Zeinelabdien T Elsherif; Dania Elsherif; Amjad M Ahmed; Husam I Ardah; Fawaz Al-Mutairi; Safeah Almaghrabi; Futun Alanazi; Hind Alaqeel; Mashael Almohaimeed; Rana Alklaib; Jawza Aldakhil; Haifa Alturki
journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
abstract:
Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is the most prevalent type of AS in developed countries. However, in developing countries, rheumatic heart disease (RHD), which has a low progression rate, remains the prevalent type. This study compared the progression rates of AS between the National Guard cohort and Western populations.
This was a retrospective single-center cohort study.
Involving patients who underwent two echocardiographic examinations within an interval of at least 2 years.
Progression of aortic valve stenosis was assessed by measuring changes in the aortic valve area (AVA), peak aortic velocity, and mean aortic valve gradient.
In total, 1669 patients (median follow-up: 6.9 years) were included in the analysis. The overall annual AVA progression rate was 0.074 ± 0.1 cm2/year (median: -0.061 cm2/year). Patients with RHD had lower progression rates than those without RHD (25%-35%; AVA: -0.036 [-0.042, -0.030] cm2/year). Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who exhibited calcific AS had the highest progression rate (AVA: -0.102 ± 0.096 cm2/year). The overall progression rate of AS for the National Guard cohort was lower across all groups compared with that in Western populations (AVA: -0.08 to 0.12 cm2/year).
Patients with ESRD who had calcific AS had the highest progression rate. Meanwhile, patients with RHD exhibited the lowest progression rate. The high prevalence of calcific AS in our study shows the importance of adherence to the American College of Cardiology/European Society of Cardiology guidelines for disease management.

title: Blue Toe Syndrome and Acute Kidney Injury Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Biopsy-Proven Case of Cholesterol Embolization Syndrome.
authors: Varun Mehta; Nelson Reyes Perez; Eleana Estrella; Shivam Joshi
abstract: Cholesterol embolization syndrome (CES) is an underrecognized complication of arterial instrumentation caused by embolization of atheromatous debris into small- and medium-sized arteries. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is well described after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but biopsy-proven CES after TAVR is rarely reported. Its delayed presentation may be mistaken for contrast-associated nephropathy, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, or systemic vasculitis. A 77-year-old man with chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral artery disease underwent transfemoral TAVR for severe aortic stenosis. Preprocedural computed tomography angiography showed a "shaggy aorta." One month later, he developed intermittent, painless violaceous discoloration of the left first through third toes. Approximately 2.5 months after TAVR, serum creatinine had risen from a baseline of 1.2-1.5 mg/dL to 4.24 mg/dL, prompting admission. Microscopic hematuria, mild eosinophilia (0.64 ×10³/µL), elevated inflammatory markers, and dysmorphic erythrocytes raised concern for glomerulonephritis and vasculitis, and empiric intravenous methylprednisolone was given while diagnostic evaluation proceeded. Kidney biopsy demonstrated atheroembolic cholesterol clefts in intrarenal arteries with ischemic changes, without glomerulonephritis or immune complex deposition. Preserved pedal pulses with an ankle-brachial index of 1.21 and toe-brachial index of 0.98 supported distal microembolization rather than large-vessel occlusion. Corticosteroids were stopped, nephrotoxins withheld, aspirin resumed, and high-intensity statin therapy was initiated; creatinine improved to approximately 3.1 mg/dL by discharge. CES should remain in the differential for progressive AKI with blue toe syndrome after TAVR, even when presentation is delayed, and initial findings suggest immune-mediated disease.

title: Left ventricular geometry as a risk factor for recurrent subaortic stenosis after primary resection.
authors: Alaa Aman Felimban; Heba Abdel-Ghafar Hessuin Mohamed; Muna Ismail; Ibrahim J Alibrahim; Husam I Ardah; Fahad Alhabshan; Mohamed Salim Kabbani
abstract:
Discrete subaortic stenosis is a progressive cause of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in children, and recurrence after surgical resection is not uncommon. We evaluated echocardiographic and morphologic factors associated with reintervention after primary subaortic membrane resection.
We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of paediatric patients (0-14 years) who underwent primary surgical resection of subaortic membrane stenosis between 2002 and 2019. Demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic variables were compared between patients requiring reintervention and those requiring a single operation. Independent predictors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
Seventy-seven patients were included; 16 required reintervention and 61 did not. On univariate analysis, the reintervention group had higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak and mean gradients and shorter membrane length. In multivariable analysis, shorter membrane length independently predicted reintervention (adjusted odds ratio 0.677 per 1-mm increase, 95% confidence interval 0.487-0.941; p = 0.020), as did higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient (adjusted odds ratio 1.066 per 1-mmHg increase, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.111; p = 0.002). A smaller aorto-septal angle showed a trend towards increased risk but did not reach statistical significance (adjusted odds ratio 0.933, 95% confidence interval 0.866-1.005; p = 0.067). Aortic regurgitation was significantly worse at follow-up in patients requiring reintervention.
Shorter subaortic membrane length and higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient were independent predictors of reintervention after primary resection. These findings may improve risk stratification and support closer echocardiographic surveillance of patients at increased risk of recurrence.

title: Does thrombocytopenia predict short-term mortality after transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement?
authors: Volkan Burak Taban; Abdullah Güner; Yakup Alsancak; Yüksel Dereli; Niyazi Görmüş
abstract:
Postprocedural thrombocytopenia is frequently observed after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and surgical aortic valve replacement (sAVR), but its independent prognostic value remains unclear. We investigated whether platelet reduction after TAVI and sAVR independently predicts short-term mortality beyond baseline procedural risk.
This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients who underwent aortic valve replacement between 2015 and 2020. Sixty-seven patients underwent TAVI and 149 underwent sAVR. Mechanical valve recipients were retained in the overall cohort but excluded from the primary TAVI-sAVR comparison. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to reduce baseline differences between groups. Longitudinal changes in platelet count (PLT), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were evaluated using generalized estimating equation models, and factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression.
The primary comparative cohort included 67 TAVI and 93 sAVR patients. After overlap weighting, adequate balance was achieved for all measured baseline covariates. Significant treatment × time interactions were observed for PLT (p = 0.001), NLR (p < 0.001), and PLR (p = 0.002). On postprocedural day 3, moderate thrombocytopenia was more frequent after sAVR than TAVI (33.5% vs. 8.3%), whereas normal platelet levels were more frequent after TAVI (45.6% vs. 8.2%; overall p < 0.001). Weighted 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between TAVI and sAVR (12.6% vs. 17.5%, p = 0.487). In Firth regression models, only EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with 90-day mortality.
Postprocedural platelet and inflammatory responses showed different temporal patterns after TAVI and sAVR. However, these biomarker changes were not independently associated with 90-day mortality after adjustment, whereas EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with mortality. Serial hematological changes should therefore be interpreted together with baseline clinical risk rather than as isolated prognostic markers.

title: Single-center clinical analysis of anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) in children: a multimodal imaging approach to risk stratification.
authors: Tao Wang; Haijie Qi; Yanli Xie; Xiaoyuan Feng; Li Gong
abstract:
This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA), explore the application of multimodal imaging in risk stratification, and establish individualized diagnosis and treatment protocols for this population.
A retrospective observational study was performed on children diagnosed with AAOCA at Wuhan Children's Hospital between January 2015 and April 2026. Clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging findings, therapeutic strategies, and long-term outcomes were comprehensively analyzed.
A total of 58 AAOCA patients confirmed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled. Initial transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) yielded false-negative results in 24 patients (41.4%). Twenty-seven patients underwent single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI, MPS), among whom 6 had normal perfusion and 21 showed perfusion defects. Seven patients with positive MPS findings received surgical correction, including 2 patients with L-AAOCA( 1 coronary angioplasty and 1 coronary unroofing) and 5 patients with R-AAOCA; all treated with coronary unroofing. No patients with negative MPS results underwent surgery, indicating that negative MPS findings perhaps provide limited valuable evidence to avoid unnecessary coronary revascularization. Two patients developed massive postoperative pericardial effusion and recovered after pericardiotomy and drainage; the remaining 5 surgical patients experienced no perioperative complications. All surgical patients were discharged after full recovery and received 3 months of aspirin antiplatelet therapy. Non-surgical patients were instructed to restrict strenuous physical activity and followed up for 3 months to 3 years. Follow-up CCTA or TTE revealed normal coronary ostia without stenosis in all patients.
Clinical manifestations of pediatric AAOCA vary widely across age groups, ranging from asymptomatic presentation to sudden cardiac arrest (SCA), leading to marked discrepancies in risk evaluation and therapeutic decision-making. Multimodal imaging including TTE, CCTA and SPECT-MPI facilitates risk stratification and guides personalized clinical management of children with AAOCA.

title: Deep Learning and Dual-Domain Fusion of Temporal and Spectrotemporal SCG for Valvular Heart Disease Classification.
authors: Junseob Kim; Tilendra Choudhary; Md Hassanuzzaman; Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
abstract: Heart valve disease (HVD) is a growing cause of cardiovascular morbidity, yet accessible screening tools remain limited. Tri-axial seismocardiogram (SCG) signals capture mechanical signatures of both stenosis and regurgitation, but their non-stationary nature and subtle inter-lesion morphological differences challenge robust classification from a single representation. This study proposes an electrocardiogram (ECG)-free dual-domain deep learning framework that combines a 1D convolutional-recurrent encoder of raw SCG waveforms with a 2D EfficientNet encoder of continuous wavelet transform scalograms, integrating temporal and spectrotemporal representations through feature-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on primary valve lesion classification in 94 patients, with an additional exploratory analysis of multi-valvular, aortic-stenosis-dominant disease. Under patient-level stratified group cross-validation, the fused model achieved the highest mean accuracy (65.3%; 95% CI, 59.8-70.7%), exceeding both unimodal encoders and the majority-class (35.2%) and covariate-only (39.1%) baselines. The same mean performance ordering was preserved when the image backbone was replaced, although the confidence intervals overlap at this cohort size. Under the segment-level protocol used in prior studies, the framework achieved 99.63% accuracy, with faster training convergence and more compact, separable feature clusters than either unimodal encoder. These findings support the value of combining temporal and spectrotemporal SCG representations and demonstrate its potential for ECG-free HVD classification under patient-independent evaluation.

title: Effects of SGLT2 inhibition on cardiac remodeling and heart failure development in aortic stenosis rats.
authors: Luana U Pagan; Mariana J Gomes; Mariana Gatto; Gustavo A F Mota; João Pedro G Oliveira; Felipe C Damatto; Lidiane M Souza; Eder A Rodrigues; Anna Clara C Santos; Gabriela H Tukiyama; Dijon H S Campos; Marcel Rodrigues Ferreira; Camila R Correa; Gilson M Murata; Bertha F Polegato; Marina P Okoshi; Katashi Okoshi
abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is increasingly prevalent in ageing populations, yet no pharmacological therapy has been shown to modify its progression to heart failure (HF). Sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve outcomes in HF, but their effects in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling remain unclear. Here, we show that rats with long-term AS develop HF features, left ventricular dilation, and systolic and diastolic dysfunction, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, impaired antioxidant defenses, myocardial fibrosis, and transcriptional remodeling. Empagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day for 8 weeks) attenuated cardiac dysfunction and reduced HF features. At molecular level, empagliflozin prevented increase in lipid peroxidation, and decreased interstitial collagen deposition, while increasing glutathione peroxidase and matrix metalloproteinase-2 activity. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,078 differentially expressed genes and revealed enrichment of pathways associated with extracellular matrix organization and signal transduction in AS. Empagliflozin predominantly regulated genes involved in cardiac contraction, mitochondrial membrane organization, apoptosis, and cell survival. Profibrotic and remodeling-associated genes were upregulated in AS, while empagliflozin induced a distinct transcriptional program associated with improved myocardial homeostasis. AS was associated with reduced activity of energy metabolism enzymes, which was not restored by empagliflozin. Collectively, these findings identify oxidative stress, extracellular matrix remodeling, and transcriptional reprogramming as mechanisms underlying cardiac dysfunction in AS. Empagliflozin mitigates cardiac remodeling and HF progression and modulates fibrosis and gene networks regulating cardiac function. These data highlight SGLT2 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy in pressure overload-induced heart failure.

title: Aortic valve replacement and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting: technical considerations in the era of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves.
authors: Dimos Karangelis; Theodora M Stougiannou
abstract:
Coexistence of severe aortic stenosis (AS) and coronary artery disease (CAD) is frequently encountered in contemporary practice, particularly amongst elderly patients with multiple comorbidities. Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combined with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an alternative strategy, surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) with concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the reference treatment for these patient groups. The introduction of sutureless and rapid-deployment aortic valves (RDAV) has considerably expanded the surgical armamentarium by facilitating implantation and reducing cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and aortic cross-clamp times. Appropriate application of these technologies requires specific technical considerations that ultimately influence operative planning and execution.
This review summarizes contemporary evidence associated with the use of sutureless and RDAVs in combined CABG and SAVR procedures. To ensure relevant literature is included, a literature search across PubMed and ScienceDirect has been carried out, spanning the last 20 years, utilizing relevant medical subject headings (MeSH) terms and keywords.
As evidence on sutureless and RDAVs technologies continues to accumulate, with associated advancements in perioperative planning, these valves are expected to become valuable adjuncts in combined procedures, by minimizing operative burden while also allowing for robust, aortic valve pathology correction.

title: Multihipposenet: multi-task deep learning for automated DDH assessment in infant hip ultrasound.
authors: Wenjing Chi; Hong Qi; Huawei Zhao; Hui Cheng; Quanlian Yuan; Shuai Zheng
abstract:
Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a common skeletal condition in infants and young children. For infants under six months, diagnosis relies on Graf ultrasonography to measure the α and β angles, which assess hip-joint development. However, this method requires experienced sonographers with expertise in complex anatomy.
In this study, we propose an end-to-end multi-task learning network that improves DDH assessment by jointly exploiting complementary anatomical information. First, we use ResNet-50 with a feature pyramid network (FPN) and a contextual semantic fusion module to extract multi-scale features from hip anatomy. Second, we employ a multi-expert gated channel transformation (ME-GCT) unit that explicitly models the relationships between tasks and channels to balance collaboration and conflict across tasks. Finally, a multi-task graph adaptive learning mechanism (MT-GALM) mines the hidden dynamic dependencies between adjacent channels across tasks. Two datasets comprising 1,355 annotated hip ultrasound images from 566 infants were constructed for this work.
Across the patient-level cross-validation test folds, 97.97% and 96.81% of the estimated α and β angles fall within 5 degrees of the expert reference.
Because validation was restricted to Graf type I and type II hips, these results should be interpreted as evidence of technical feasibility rather than of established clinical utility; evaluation on type III and type IV hips is required before clinical deployment.

title: A field-acquired tea leaf image dataset for disease and pest-damage classification in Bangladesh.
authors: Sakibul Hasan Chowdhury; Md Shohel Arman
abstract: This data article presents a field-acquired collection of 2500 tea-leaf photographs from four tea-growing locations in Chunarughat, Habiganj, Bangladesh, collected between April 07 and June 23, 2025. The repository contains four image-level categories: Blight (Brown and Gray Blight combined; 555 images), Red Rust (620 images), Helopeltis damage (675 images), and finally Healthy Leaf (650 images). Images were captured under naturally varying illumination, leaf orientation, and background conditions and were retained at their available photographic dimensions. The deposited JPEG images retain their original spatial characteristics, with seven distinct resolutions ranging from 1200 × 1600 to 4608 × 3456 pixels (2411 portrait and 89 landscape images; no square images). The collection was acquired using multiple smartphones and preserves natural field backgrounds rather than standardized laboratory scenes. Manual visual quality screening was used to exclude substantially blurred, unclear, and obvious repeated captures, while no artificial augmentation was applied to the deposited files. The principal contribution of the dataset is the release and documentation of the complete 2500-image field repository for disease- and pest-damage classification; an approximately balanced 2000-image subset was previously used for downstream deep-learning experiments. The complete dataset is openly available through Mendeley Data under a CC BY 4.0 license.

title: Addressing unmet clinical needs in treatment-resistant breast cancer: expanding the diagnostic-prognostic landscape through next-generation inflammatory signatures.
authors: Emmanuel Ifeanyi Obeagu
abstract: Treatment-resistant breast cancer remains a major clinical challenge because conventional clinicopathological and molecular biomarkers incompletely capture the dynamic interactions between tumour cells, immunity, inflammation, and the systemic host response. Next-generation inflammatory signatures offer an opportunity to expand the diagnostic-prognostic landscape by integrating cellular, molecular, immune, and thromboinflammatory indicators with established tumour characteristics. This narrative review critically examines emerging evidence for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, C-reactive protein, cytokines, tumour-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, neutrophil extracellular traps, coagulation biomarkers, and liquid-biopsy-derived measures in treatment-resistant breast cancer. Particular attention is given to sources of heterogeneity, including population characteristics, tumour subtype, treatment exposure, comorbid inflammation, sampling time, specimen processing, analytical platforms, and inconsistent biomarker thresholds. The review further evaluates the transition from biomarker discovery to clinical decision support, highlighting the need for prospective multicentre validation, standardised analytical procedures, external validation of computational models, and integration with molecular subtyping, circulating tumour DNA, imaging, and immune profiling. Rather than interpreting inflammation as a static prognostic variable, longitudinal inflammatory trajectories may provide earlier signals of biological treatment resistance and complement conventional measures of disease progression. Future research should establish clinically actionable inflammatory combinations and evaluate biomarker-guided anti-inflammatory strategies alongside standard therapies. Ultimately, integrating inflammatory phenotypes with tumour molecular characteristics may facilitate earlier recognition of resistance and more precise, dynamic, and equitable breast cancer management.

title: Cascaded deep learning for synthesis of 18F-FDG PET from 18F-octreotide: model parameter optimization and performance evaluation.
authors: Ruxi Chang; Liping Yang; Jungang Gao; Xiang Liu; Bo Wang; Yan Li; Xiaoyi Duan
abstract:
To investigate a cascaded conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN)-based method for synthesizing 18F-FDG PET images from 18F-octreotide, optimize model parameter configurations, and evaluate the quality of the synthesized images.
Imaging data from 71 tumor patients who underwent dual-tracer PET/CT examinations with 18F-FDG and 18F-octreotide between May 2022 and November 2025 were retrospectively collected. A cascaded deep learning architecture (first stage: 3D U-Net; second stage: self-attention 3D V-Net) was employed to evaluate the effects of image preprocessing, resampling size, and patch size on synthesis quality. Three preprocessing strategies (log transformation, normalization, and a combined approach) were compared. Image quality was assessed using five objective metrics (SSIM, PSNR, MSE, MAE, and NMI) and Likert 5-point ratings from three nuclear medicine physicians; liver and lesion-level SUV agreement were further evaluated.
In the held-out test cohort (n = 14), the combined preprocessing method (log transformation + normalization) significantly outperformed the individual methods (SSIM: 0.8454 ± 0.0328 vs. 0.7831 ± 0.0337 vs. 0.7438 ± 0.0362, P < 0.001). On the identical held-out test cohort (n = 14), the Group 2 parameter configuration (resampling size: 256 × 256 × 512; patch size: 128 × 128 × 128) outperformed Group 1, with an SSIM of 0.8854 ± 0.0455 and a PSNR of 28.15 ± 3.35 dB, representing relative improvements of 19.1% and 83.5%, respectively, over Group 1 (paired-samples t-test, both P < 0.001). The mean Likert score was 4.53 ± 0.19. Quantitative analysis of liver SUVmean showed no significant difference between synthesized and real images (P = 0.967, paired t-test). Lesion-level quantitative analysis demonstrated high agreement between synthetic and real 18F-FDG images, with Pearson correlation coefficients of 1.0000, 0.9995, and 0.9991 for SUVmax and SUVmean (n = 14) and SUVpeak (n = 13), respectively (all P < 0.001), no significant differences on paired t-tests (all P > 0.05), and all Bland-Altman differences within the 95% limits of agreement.
The cascaded deep learning model enabled cross-tracer synthesis from 18F-octreotide to 18F-FDG PET images. In this exploratory, single-center pilot cohort, the optimized configuration demonstrated promising quantitative and visual performance, supporting image-synthesis feasibility and potential clinical utility of a single-injection, dual-parameter molecular imaging approach for neuroendocrine tumors. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before any clinical application.

title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
authors: Zehui Li; Xin Duan; Junjie Lian; Xuan Li; Qian Liang; Xu Liu; Yan Tan; Guoqiang Yang; Jiangfeng Du; Lina Wu; Xiaochun Wang; Hui Zhang
abstract:
High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients.
A Transformer-based multimodal fusion model was proposed. Key tumor regions were identified from whole-slide pathology images via weakly supervised clustering, and pathological features were extracted using attention-based multiple instance learning. Concurrently, 2.5D tumor subregional features were derived from multiparametric MRI sequences. These multimodal features were deeply fused using a Transformer encoder. The model was developed and validated on a multicenter cohort (504 patients), and its biological basis was explored through transcriptomic analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction networks, and immune deconvolution.
The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.910, 0.861, and 0.833 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis implicated DNA damage repair processes in high-benefit patients, suggesting that enhanced DNA repair capacity may contribute to TMZ sensitivity. Immune deconvolution showed higher M1 macrophage infiltration and lower regulatory T cell abundance in the high-benefit group, consistent with a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Importantly, low-benefit patients who completed TMZ chemotherapy had shorter survival than those treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone or surgery alone.
This model identifies patients unlikely to benefit from standard TMZ chemotherapy, providing a tool for postoperative personalized treatment stratification and optimization of therapeutic strategies in HGGs.

title: MSFANet: a multi-scale feature aggregation network for tobacco pest recognition.
authors: Shun He; Sifan Li; Xinjian Li; Qianqian Luo; Sufen Dong; Lu Lei; Xingjiang Chen; Liuti Cai; Jianyu Meng; Ning Lu; Hancheng Wang
abstract:
Tobacco is a globally significant economic crop, and pest infestation represents one of the primary factors contributing to declines in both yield and quality. However, tobacco pests encompass a wide variety of species that differ substantially in morphology and scale. Field-captured images are frequently subject to complex background interference and class imbalance, presenting considerable challenges for automated recognition. Existing deep learning approaches remain limited in their capacity for multi-scale feature extraction and discriminative feature representation under such conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi-Scale Feature Aggregation Network (MSFANet) for tobacco pest recognition, formulated here as a single-label image classification task.
To address scale variation and complex field backgrounds, two task-oriented modules were developed. The Multi-Scale Pyramid Pooling (MSPP) module aggregates contextual information across multiple receptive fields through parallel feature extraction and adaptive cross-branch fusion. The Hierarchical Feature Fusion Block (HFFB) subsequently refines the feature representations through spatial gating and partial convolution. An auxiliary classification head and Focal Loss were incorporated during training to provide intermediate supervision and address class imbalance, respectively.
The effectiveness of MSFANet was evaluated on a dataset comprising 13 tobacco-associated pest and natural-enemy categories. The model achieved accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 97.63%, 97.89%, 97.59%, and 97.71%, respectively, with a parameter count of 1.21 M. Among the models trained from random initialization, MSFANet shared the highest accuracy while using the fewest parameters.
By combining multi-scale contextual aggregation with hierarchical feature refinement, MSFANet achieved accurate classification across the 13 tobacco-associated categories under complex field conditions. The proposed method provides effective technical support for automated and precision-oriented pest monitoring in tobacco fields, offering practical value for advancing precise pest management and the broader development of smart agriculture.

title: A quantum-inspired cross-attention fusion network for multi-class eye disease classification from retinal fundus images.
authors: Abinash P; Krishnamoorthy N
abstract: Automated screening of blinding eye diseases from colour fundus photographs is an active area of medical image analysis, yet many reported systems are validated on a single dataset and offer limited insight into their internal decision process. This study introduces QICAF-Net, a dual-branch deep learning framework that couples a Swin Transformer global-context branch with an EfficientNet local-lesion branch and fuses their representations through a novel Quantum-Inspired Cross-Attention Fusion (QICAF) module. The QICAF module reformulates cross-attention using the mathematical formalism of quantum states: token features are amplitude-encoded as complex unit vectors, transformed by a learnable norm-preserving unitary gate, compared through a fidelity-inspired similarity, normalised by a Born-rule measurement rule, and combined through an entanglement-inspired bilinear interaction. All operations are executed as classical linear algebra on conventional graphics hardware; no physical quantum computer and no quantum speed-up are claimed. The model was trained and evaluated on a balanced four-class retinal dataset of 4,217 fundus images spanning cataract, diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma and normal categories. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation with six-view test-time augmentation (TTA), QICAF-Net attained a macro-F1 of 0.9358 ± 0.0113, an accuracy of 0.9367 ± 0.0112 and a macro one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9914 ± 0.0023; a three-seed evaluation of the full model gave a macro-F1 of 0.9420 ± 0.0071. An 18-run multi-seed component ablation (six fusion configurations × three seeds) confirmed that the quantum-inspired components achieve accuracy statistically indistinguishable from strong classical fusion baselines, and a paired three-seed significance test between QICAF-Net and a matched dual-branch concatenation model returned no statistically significant accuracy difference (paired t-test p = 0.887; Wilcoxon p = 1.000). Against five single-backbone baselines under an identical preprocessing and TTA protocol, QICAF-Net was competitive but did not exceed the strongest backbones (Swin-Tiny 0.9583, ViT-Small 0.9487). The principal contribution of the module is therefore a novel and interpretable formulation rather than a raw accuracy gain. External validation on a heterogeneous independent cohort (N = 3,907) showed heterogeneous cross-dataset transfer - better preserved for cataract and normal and substantially degraded for glaucoma; under an observed external-domain shift the diabetic-retinopathy sensitivity fell to 39.61%, and under colour-constancy correction with six-view TTA the external accuracy was 0.8741 (95% CI 0.8633-0.8841) and the macro-F1 0.7188 (95% CI 0.6969-0.7398). Two complementary explainability methods together with visualisation of the QICAF attention indicated that the model attends to clinically plausible regions, most strongly the optic nerve head for glaucoma. Calibration, quantitative explanation-faithfulness (deletion/insertion) and profiler-based computational analyses were additionally performed. QICAF-Net is thus presented as an interpretable and transparently evaluated framework whose accuracy is on par with established fusion strategies while contributing a new attention formulation to the retinal imaging literature.

title: Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study.
authors: Yixing Li; Dehui Liu; Ruixue Qin; Xingchang Li; Mei Li
abstract:
Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level.
Age-standardized thyroid cancer incidence was the prespecified primary outcome. We aimed to (1) build machine learning models predicting country-level thyroid cancer incidence from dietary and socioeconomic features, (2) quantify confounder-adjusted dietary associations with incidence, including prespecified sensitivity analyses of the iodine-rich food availability index, and (3) identify key dietary predictors through explainability analyses and a descriptive decomposition of the development pathway. Mortality was analyzed only as a secondary outcome in order to evaluate whether the incidence patterns could be attributed to differential cancer detection rather than to differences in disease occurrence.
We integrated GLOBOCAN 2022 (cancer outcomes), FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (113 food items, 2010-2022; primary exposure 2015-2019 mean), the UNDP Human Development Report 2025 statistical annex (HDI 2023 and its life expectancy, education, and income sub-indices), and WHO obesity prevalence (2022) across 163 countries, yielding 155 harmonized variables and 150 numeric predictors. All modeling was performed inside a nested cross-validation framework: multiple imputation by chained equations, standardization, four-method consensus feature selection, and hyperparameter search were fitted exclusively on the training partition of each outer fold (10 folds × five repetitions), and performance was summarized from pooled out-of-fold predictions with 95% confidence intervals obtained by resampling countries (2,000 bootstrap replicates). Three analyses separated dietary signal from confounding: block-wise models comparing socioeconomic-only, diet-only and combined feature sets; leave-one-region-out validation across six world regions; and confounder-adjusted partial correlations under a basic (HDI, obesity) and an extended adjustment set (HDI, obesity, the three HDI sub-indices, and region fixed effects), with Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni correction applied across all comparisons. Iodine-related exposure was represented by an iodine-rich food availability index constructed from seafood, dairy, and egg supply; its construction was interrogated in four sensitivity analyses in which the components were entered separately and jointly, four weighting schemes were compared, total animal protein supply was added to the adjustment set, and an iodine-poor animal-origin food index was used as a specificity control. Binary classification and all mortality analyses were secondary.
Regression on incidence was the primary task. Stacking ensemble performed best, with a pooled out-of-fold R² of 0.613 (95% CI [0.510, 0.726]), RMSE = 3.04, MAE = 1.82, and Spearman ρ = 0.901 (95% CI [0.862, 0.924]); random forest (R² = 0.609), bagging (R² = 0.599), and KNN (R² = 0.580) followed, and a high-dimensional deep tabular model (DynaTab) was statistically comparable (R² = 0.626). Predictive accuracy was, however, almost entirely socioeconomic: nine development variables alone gave R² = 0.609, 140 dietary variables alone gave 0.284, and the incremental contribution of the dietary block was -0.048 (95% CI -0.169 to +0.034), +0.021, and +0.017 across model families. Under leave-one-region-out validation, the rank ordering of countries was largely preserved (pooled ρ = 0.813), but the level was not. Unadjusted associations with incidence were positive for the iodine-rich food availability index (ρ = 0.234), total energy (ρ = 0.230), seafood (ρ = 0.219), and the animal-to-plant protein ratio (ρ = 0.221). After adjustment and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, seafood supply, dairy supply, the iodine-rich food availability index, the animal-to-plant protein ratio, and mollusks remained significant under the extended adjustment set (seafood partial r = 0.196, q = 0.031; iodine-rich food availability index 0.224, q = 0.026), whereas plant protein did not (-0.095, q = 0.309). In sensitivity analyses, the index association was carried by seafood (0.196, q = 0.017) and dairy (0.198, q = 0.017) but not eggs (0.065, q = 0.411), was stable across equal-weighted, z-score, and iodine-content-weighted constructions (0.238-0.256), survived further adjustment for total animal protein supply (0.203, q = 0.032), and was not reproduced by an iodine-poor animal-origin food index (0.102, q = 0.198). Path decomposition attributed 50.2% of the seafood-incidence correlation to the HDI pathway (95% bootstrap CI 16%-90%). In the secondary mortality analysis, the dietary ordering was preserved, but associations with the mortality-to-incidence ratio were close to zero (HDI ρ = 0.053; seafood ρ = 0.065), and in the sensitivity classification analysis, Extra Trees reached AUC = 0.932 (95% CI [0.893, 0.964]) at the median split.
With all model construction confined to training folds, machine learning models built from national food supply and socioeconomic data explain a moderate share of the between-country variation in thyroid cancer incidence, but that predictive accuracy is carried by development indicators rather than by diet. The availability of iodine-rich food groups, seafood supply, and the animal-to-plant protein ratio nevertheless retained positive ecological associations with incidence after adjustment for development and metabolic confounders and after correction for multiple comparisons, and the index association proved robust to how the index was constructed and specific to iodine-rich rather than to animal-origin food groups in general; plant protein showed no association once multiplicity was controlled. Roughly half of the seafood-incidence correlation tracks the development pathway, and the secondary mortality analysis is consistent with a substantial contribution from differential detection. These findings are ecological associations with the availability of iodine-rich food groups, not with measured iodine intake or exposure; they generate testable hypotheses for individual-level studies with measured iodine status and do not establish causation.

title: An attention-guided dense convolutional network for automated diabetic foot ulcer segmentation.
authors: Rampriya R S; Sabari Nathan; Arumuga Arun R
abstract:
A large number of diabetic patients have diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), and it is essential to segment the regions of the ulcer in a timely and accurate manner to treat them. The segmentation task is very difficult due to the highly irregular shape of the ulcers and very small areas of lesions, up to 0.04% of the DFU image.
We aim to develop an attention-guided dense convolutional network, called UlcerNet, which is able to extract fine-grained ulcer features at different scales. It introduces dense convolutions, multi-scale residual attention blocks (MRADB), and modified receptive-field modules (MRFB) to enhance feature propagation and context modeling. We use the public DFUC 2022 dataset that contains 4000 close-up foot images to train and evaluate the UlcerNet model.
Our model is able to perform a Dice of 73.50% and mIoU of 76.04%, which gives better performance than the standard segmentation baselines (FCN8 49.93%, SegNet 47.68%, DeepLabV3 + 62.77%) and recent DFU segmentation baselines (TranUNet 42.61%, HarDNet-DFUS 59.81%, UFOS-Net 73.09%).
An ablation study further shows that each component, such as dense blocks, channel attention, spatial attention, MRADB, and MRFB, is significant for the accuracy. These findings show that UlcerNet offers good and precise DFU segmentation, which can be useful for clinical settings in the real-world.

title: Large language models in spirometry interpretation: impact of guideline-based prompting.
authors: Muazzez Elçin Özkan; Damla Serçe Unat; Ömer Selim Unat; Mutlu Onur Güçsav; Mukaddes Hande Özgen; Dilara Özdemir; Erdal İlhan; Orhan Meral; Onur Akçay
abstract:
To compare the performance of ChatGPT and Gemini with pulmonologist assessment in spirometry interpretation based on European Respiratory Society and American Thoracic Society (ERS/ATS) standards and to evaluate the effect of structured guideline-based prompting on diagnostic accuracy.
This cross-sectional diagnostic study involved 500 anonymized spirometry reports. Quality control (QC) assessment and ventilatory pattern classification were based on pulmonologist consensus as the reference standard. The same cases were evaluated by ChatGPT and Gemini before and after structured guideline-based prompting derived from ERS/ATS criteria. Analyses were restricted to 362 tests deemed interpretable by all groups. Agreement was assessed with McNemar and McNemar-Bowker tests, and diagnostic performance was evaluated with class-specific and overall multiclass measures.
Both models correctly extracted all numerical spirometric parameters but overestimated test interpretability compared with specialists (all P<0.001). Among the 362 tests interpretable by all groups, ChatGPT's overall multiclass accuracy increased from 72.1% to 74.0% after prompting (κ=0.582 to 0.608), whereas Gemini's accuracy remained 69.9% (κ=0.552 in both phases). ChatGPT's sensitivity for obstructive patterns increased from 60.0% to 63.6%, whereas Gemini's decreased from 32.7% to 19.1%; sensitivity for mixed patterns remained low. Errors predominantly involved misclassification of obstructive patterns as restrictive or mixed.
Guideline-based prompting produced model-specific and class-specific effects rather than a uniform improvement in diagnostic performance. Neither model reliably differentiated all ventilatory patterns. These findings support specialist-supervised, human-in-the-loop use and warrant standardized validation before clinical or medicolegal implementation.

title: A Large Language Model Framework for Seed Implant Brachytherapy: Adaptive Weight Optimization via Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
authors: Zhuo Xiao; Qinglong Yao; Jingjing Wang; Bo Liu; Fugen Zhou; Haitao Sun; Zhe Ji; Yuliang Jiang; Junjie Wang; Qiuwen Wu
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
abstract: Seed implant brachytherapy (SIBT) is an effective cancer treatment modality; however, clinical planning often relies on manual adjustment of objective function weights, leading to inefficiencies and suboptimal results. This study proposes an adaptive weight optimization framework for SIBT planning, driven by large language models (LLMs). A locally deployed DeepSeek-R1 LLM is integrated with an automatic planning algorithm in an iterative loop. Starting with fixed weights, the LLM evaluates plan quality and recommends new weights in the next iteration. This process continues until convergence criteria are met, after which the LLM conducts a comprehensive evaluation to identify the optimal plan. A clinical knowledge base, constructed and queried via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), enhances the model's domain-specific reasoning. The proposed method was retrospectively validated on 23 patient cases who underwent head-and-neck SIBT, showing that the LLM-assisted approach maintained clinical target volume (CTV) coverage and reduced excessive target dose relative to fixed-weight planning; in the eight patients with available organs at risk (OARs) contours, OAR dose metrics showed favorable numerical trends. The study demonstrates the potential of LLMs as assistive tools for SIBT planning under clinician supervision.

title: Physics-guided deep neural networks for Laguerre-Gaussian modal decomposition via PCA-ranked Zernike descriptors.
authors: Malihe Karami; Saeed Ghavami Sabouri
abstract: Direct pixel-space learning for Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modal decomposition suffers from high input dimensionality and severe computational redundancy. Here, we present a physics-guided framework that maps intensity patterns into a compact Zernike descriptor space coupled to a deep neural network (DNN). Using principal component analysis (PCA), we systematically interrogate the effective dimensionality of the sampled Zernike feature space and establish a variance-weighted ranking for Zernike features. Experimental validation using a digital micromirror device (DMD)-based setup demonstrates that dominant descriptors capture >99% of dataset variance. Truncated feature subsets achieve saturated reconstruction fidelity (∼ 98%) and near-unity spatial correlation under realistic optical perturbations. This framework eliminates full-resolution image processing, paving the way for potential real-time optical mode sorting applications.

title: Probe-aware self-supervised neural network for X-ray holographic reconstruction.
authors: Jiarui Hu; Yu Hu; Guangcai Chang; Lei Wang; Bin Ji; Jingyan Shi
abstract: X-ray phase contrast imaging based on propagation is a crucial technique for achieving non-destructive detection at the micro- and nano-scales. However, the recovery of phase information from intensity measurements presents a typical ill-posed inverse problem. Traditional iterative algorithms often necessitate multi-distance measurements, which increases both the complexity and time cost of experiments. Although deep learning has introduced a novel paradigm for phase retrieval, supervised methods depend on paired data that are challenging to obtain. Furthermore, existing approaches frequently ignore wavefront distortion of the illumination probe, leading to significant background artifacts in reconstruction results. To address these challenges, we propose a probe-aware self-supervised neural network (PASNet), designed to jointly estimate the complex object and probe wavefields from single-distance holograms for phase reconstruction. PASNet employs a compact U-Net architecture that takes as joint input holograms representing "object + probe" and "probe only." A physically-driven loss function is utilized to integrate the Fresnel diffraction into the network optimization process, enabling self-supervised learning without requiring labeled data. Evaluation on simulated and experimental datasets demonstrates that PASNet effectively decouples object and probe wavefronts while suppressing background artifacts. With only single-distance double-exposure, our proposed method achieves superior phase structural fidelity and background stability compared with traditional iterative algorithms and other neural networks. Additionally, robustness analysis indicates that PASNet maintains strong performance across varying propagation distances and noise levels.

title: Simultaneous misalignment and mode mismatch sensing in resonant optical cavities using intensity-only measurements.
authors: Liu Tao; Eleonora Capocasa; Yuhang Zhao; Jacques Ding; Isander Ahrend; Matteo Barsuglia
abstract: Precise sensing and control of spatial mode content is essential for the performance of precision optical systems, particularly interferometric gravitational-wave detectors, where misalignment and mode mismatch can lead to significant optical losses and degraded quantum noise suppression. Conventional approaches, including heterodyne wavefront sensing and phase camera techniques, are effective but can be limited by hardware complexity and systematic uncertainties arising from restricted reference-beam overlap. This paper presents what we believe to be a novel two-step deep learning pipeline for robust beam diagnostics based solely on beam intensity images. In the first stage, a multi-intensity-image convolutional neural network (CNN) performs accurate mode decomposition, recovering the complex modal content of distorted beams. In the second stage, the predicted mode coefficients are fed into a downstream regression network that simultaneously estimates all eight degrees of freedom (DoFs) associated with misalignment and mode mismatch, including beam tilt, lateral offset, and waist size and position mismatches in both transverse directions. The proposed CNN-based framework achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0034 in the mode decomposition stage, which propagates to a total MAE of 0.0062 in the recovered beam imperfection parameters at the final stage on a numerically generated synthetic dataset. This corresponds to an average residual optical loss of 39 ppm per DoF (310 ppm total). This approach relies only on standard CCD imaging and is robust to random intensity noise, eliminating the need for complex interferometric hardware. The results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning pipeline enables real-time, high-accuracy wavefront sensing and mode-mismatch diagnostics, providing a hardware-efficient tool for improving the stability and sensitivity of precision optical systems.

title: Sensor-aware physical modelling for deep learning-based single-photon imaging.
authors: Yiwei Chen; Xun Lang; Yu Pan
abstract: Deep learning-based single-photon imaging commonly relies on synthetic time-resolved histograms with incompletely specified sensing physics. We present a sensor-aware framework that represents the source-receiver response, spatially varying background, detector artifacts, and first-detection acquisition within a family of photon measurement operators. A controlled cross-condition protocol independently varies the sensing operators used for training and testing, enabling systematic evaluation of sensing-model mismatch across four representative reconstruction networks. An operator-induced risk formulation connects sensing perturbations to changes in reconstruction error and model ranking, while Monte Carlo verification, parameter-sensitivity analysis, and comparison with measured single-photon data provide complementary numerical and physical validation. Under C4 testing, matched C4 training reduces the architecture-averaged mean absolute error by 22.3% relative to C0 training. This effect persists in the same-dataset NYUv2 control, although with reduced magnitude. Experiments on measured WISC photon data further show pronounced architecture-dependent transfer across training sensing conditions. These results establish a reproducible framework for quantifying how sensing-model fidelity and reconstruction architecture jointly determine single-photon imaging performance.

title: Symplectic-inspired neural operators for discretization-invariant light propagation with exact power conservation.
authors: Rui Yu; Jining Li; Qingmingyang Zhou; Dong Wang; Shimin Yang; Zhen Xu; Kai Chen; Degang Xu
abstract: Computational optics faces a dilemma between the prohibitive cost of split-step Fourier methods and the numerical dissipation of deep-learning surrogates. Neither paradigm simultaneously achieves physical fidelity, computational efficiency, and end-to-end differentiability. We introduce the Symplectic-inspired Neural Operator (SympNO), a physics-enforced architecture that embeds the symplectic Strang splitting structure into the network. A hard unitary constraint ensures optical power preservation to machine precision, eliminating soft penalty terms. By learning data-driven, effective corrections to splitting errors over macro-scale steps, SympNO achieves a Pareto-optimal balance between accuracy and latency. It outperforms the finest beam-propagation configuration in both NMSE and inference time, and remains the only compared method that is simultaneously differentiable, mesh-generalizable, and physically consistent. The Iterative SympNO Solver (ISS) extends this to high-fidelity multi-step propagation, achieving cross-wavelength generalization and consistent accuracy across spatial scales (642 to 40962) without retraining. In strong turbulence (σ R 2≈1), the ISS reproduces reference statistics with NMSE <10-4. For inverse design in thick random media, the differentiable surrogate enables gradient-based optimization with diffraction efficiency within 2% of the physics-informed BPM upper bound while reducing forward steps by 15 ×. These results demonstrate that embedding geometric conservation into neural operators unifies computational efficiency with physical accuracy in Hamiltonian wave systems, offering a robust simulation tool for real-time atmospheric optics and nanophotonic device design.

title: Prioritizing soil Pb verification targets under spatial outer testing for regional monitoring.
authors: Wenjing Sun; Chichen Zhou; Ridong Fan; Lin Li; Anchun Cheng; Jinkun Huang; Xunchang Fei; Behzad Fatahi
abstract: Regional soil Pb monitoring must decide which samples to verify first under a fixed budget. We distinguish contamination status, screening status, and verification priority; the model ranks verification targets using labels defined by prespecified screening rules rather than confirmed contamination. Using 33,004 label-applicable samples, we excluded Pb concentration, screening thresholds, label-source identifiers, and spatial split identifiers from the predictor set. Candidate models were selected by grouped out-of-fold evaluation in the development set and tested in held-out 50 km × 50 km spatial blocks. CatBoost achieved an outer-test PR-AUC of 0.4300. Under a 15% verification budget, the 1036-sample priority list captured 330 of 441 samples classified as high risk by the screening rules (74.83%), with a 31.85% within-list rate and 4.99-fold enrichment. Restricting development to the dominant USGS component retained 73.51% top-15% capture, with strong rank agreement to the integrated model (Spearman ρ = 0.8977). Sensitivity analyses separated stable, rule-sensitive, proxy-sensitive, and dual-sensitive candidates. The resulting ranking supports phased verification within the evaluated rule and data domain; broader transfer requires independent confirmation.

title: Host genomic context determines the direction of an oracle-predicted sequence effect: a composition-preserving CpG intervention in Enformer and Borzoi.
authors: Selahattin Alperen Uysal
abstract: Sequence-to-function models are increasingly used as oracles to score designed regulatory elements, on the untested assumption that an effect measured at one locus holds at another. Taking chromatin and host loci from multiple sclerosis risk regions, we kept four questions apart: sequence realism, transfer of discrimination, edit stability, calibration. A sixth-order Markov chain reproduced the cell-type-specific motif enrichment a trained transformer missed, despite its lower held-out likelihood. Scores differ in level between loci far more than between inserts at one locus, yet inserts selected by an Enformer-derived index kept 85% of their advantage at four unseen loci. Once GC was matched, however, the index separated peak-derived from inaccessible sequence at none of 12 hosts, and from random sequence in opposite directions at different hosts. Placing identical inserts and an identical CpG edit at 24 host loci, the effect varied far beyond sampling noise on host identity alone ([Formula: see text]), unpredicted by 18 host properties. It survives scoring only the bins the insert occupies ([Formula: see text], and across 200 loci), so is no artefact of aggregation; the apparent host dominance, however, falls from 25-fold to 3-fold under that localised score, and the one locus positive under the whole-window score reverses under it. Borzoi reproduced the heterogeneity but not its amplitude, and the objective did not predict lentiMPRA activity. For these two oracles and this edit, the size of a predicted effect depends on where it is measured, and its direction at any one locus is not robust.

title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis.
authors: Jiasui Liu; Simon Schäfer; Svenja Lehnung; Lukas Max Baumann; Lars Mühlberg; Cornelia Steiner; Markus Schreiber; Mark Linder; Sonja Welsch; Fan Liu; Boris Bogdanow; Jacomina Krijnse Locker; Beata Turoňová
abstract: It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
authors: Niklas Grieger; Jannik Raskob; Siamak Mehrkanoon; Stephan Bialonski
abstract: Sleep is essential for health, yet studying its dynamics requires manual sleep staging, a labor-intensive step in research and clinical care. Across centers, polysomnography (PSG) recordings are traditionally scored in 30-s epochs for pragmatic, not physiological, reasons and vary in electrode count, montage, and subject characteristics. These constraints challenge harmonized multi-center studies and the discovery of robust biomarkers on shorter timescales. We present AnySleep, a deep neural network that scores sleep from any electroencephalography (EEG) or electrooculography (EOG) data at adjustable temporal resolutions. We trained and validated the model on over 20,000 overnight recordings (>200,000 h of EEG and EOG) from 28 datasets across multiple clinics to promote robust generalization across sites. The model attains state-of-the-art performance and surpasses or equals established baselines at 30-s epochs. Performance improves with more channels, yet remains strong when EOG is absent, or only EOG or single EEG derivations (frontal, central, or occipital) are available. On sub-30-s timescales, the model captures short wake intrusions consistent with arousals and improves the prediction of pathophysiological conditions (obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, insomnia) over 30-s scoring. We make the model publicly available to facilitate large-scale studies with heterogeneous electrode setups and accelerate biomarker discovery in sleep.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD.
