title: Trends in rheumatic heart disease mortality in the United States of America from 1968 to 2023: a nationwide analysis
authors: Jacky Chen; Dean Nelson; Adam Trytell; Andrew Burns; Noel Bayley; Elizabeth Davida Paratz
abstract: Abstract Background Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a preventable sequela of acute rheumatic fever causing chronic valvular damage to the heart. In the United States of America (USA), RHD persists among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. This study examines long-term trends in RHD mortality from 1968 to 2023, identifying associated demographic and geographic factors to guide targeted public health interventions. Methods This retrospective observational study examined death certificate data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Wide-Ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (WONDER) database, encompassing three different International Classification of Disease periods (ICD-8, ICD-9, ICD-10). Analysis included stratification by age, gender, race, ethnicity and urbanisation level. Joinpoint analysis and multiple regression analysis were used to identify trends. Results RHD mortality declined significantly from 1968 to 2012, with falling crude mortality rates in both sexes and large reductions in absolute deaths among White individuals and adults aged 55–74 years. From 2012 to 2023, total deaths increased from 3,083 to 4,332, crude mortality rose from 0.98 to 1.29 per 100,000 and age-adjusted mortality increased from 0.88 to 1.04 per 100,000 (all p < 0.0001). Increases were observed across sex, race, ethnicity, urbanisation, and most age subgroups. Females had consistently higher RHD crude mortality rate ratios than men (1.09–2.43). The age distribution of RHD mortality shifted markedly over the study period, with deaths among individuals aged ≥ 75 years increasing from 17% in 1968 to 61% in 2023. Race- and ethnicity-specific CMR increased across all assessed groups from 2012 to 2023, with the largest relative increases among American Indian or Alaska Native individuals (+ 112.4%; β = 0.033 per 100,000/year, p = 0.002) and Hispanic individuals (+ 60.2%; β = 0.014 per 100,000/year, p < 0.001). Conclusion Following decades of decline, RHD mortality in the United States increased after 2012. Our study identified a persistent female predominance in RHD mortality and a marked shift in mortality burden from middle-aged adults towards older populations.

title: Segmental jejunal “watermelon-like” vascular ectasia in portal hypertensive enteropathy: rationale for medical therapy over argon plasma coagulation
authors: Joel Omar Jáquez-Quintana; Ana Sofía Garza-González; Darhy Eunice Garcia-Bravo; Julio Alexis Arce-Hernández; Francisco Bosques‐Padilla
abstract: Introduction: Small bowel angiodysplasias account for over 50% of causes of small bowel bleeding and carry a worse prognosis than lesions located elsewhere in the gastrointestinal tract.Re-bleeding rates are high even after first-line endoscopic therapy and are associated with high levels of morbidity for affected patients.Small trials of long-acting somatostatin analogues have shown promising results but have not yet been assessed in patients with refractory small bowel disease.Aim: The purpose of this study was to assess the effect of long-acting somatostatin analogues in reducing re-bleeding rates and transfusion requirements, and improving haemoglobin levels in patients with refractory small bowel angiodysplasia.Methods: Patients with refractory small bowel angiodysplasia were treated with 20 mg of long-acting octreotide for a minimum of three months.Response was assessed according to: rates of re-bleeding, haemoglobin levels, transfusion requirements, and side effects.Results: A total of 24 patients were initially treated and 20 received at least three doses.Rates of complete, partial and nonresponse were 70%, 20% and 10% respectively.Average haemoglobin rates increased from 9.19 g/dl to 11.35 g/dl (p ¼ 0.0027, 95% confidence interval (CI) À3.5 to À1.1) in the group overall and 70% remained transfusion-free after a mean treatment duration of 8.8 months.The rate of adverse events was higher than previously reported at 30%.Conclusion: Long-acting somatostatin analogues offer a therapeutic advantage in a significant proportion of patients with small bowel angiodysplasia.With careful patient selection and close observation, a long-acting somatostatin analogue should be considered in all patients with persistent anaemia attributable to refractory disease in conjunction with other standard treatments.

title: Central nervous system involvement in relapsing polychondritis with inflammatory changes in the cerebrospinal fluid and cranial MRI abnormalities: a case series report
authors: Jie Chen; Zhewen Luo; Ping Hua; Biying Wang; Xing Wang
abstract: Objective To explore the clinical features of relapsing polychondritis (RP) with central nervous system (CNS) involvement as the major manifestation. Methods A total of 11 RP patients who were hospitalized in the Department of Neurology, the Affiliated Brain Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2020 to December 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. Their clinical manifestations, laboratory indicators, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) changes, and cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings were comprehensively analyzed. Results CNS involvement was the major initial manifestation in the vast majority of RP patients (90.9%, 10/11), as cognitive impairment ( n = 10), headache ( n = 7), psychiatric/behavioral symptoms ( n = 6), epileptic seizures ( n = 4), limb numbness ( n = 4), limb weakness ( n = 4), and limb tremor ( n = 3). CSF analysis revealed an inflammatory response in the CNS, as evidenced by increased levels of neutrophils, albumin, and immunoglobulins at varying degrees. White matter degeneration ( n = 7) and brain atrophy ( n = 7) were the pronounced changes on cranial MRI. Brain lesions were mainly distributed in the cortex, subcortex, and infratentorium. Parenchymal or meningeal enhancement was observed on MRI scans in three RP patients with CNS involvement. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) detected three cases of hypoperfusion and two cases of hyperperfusion in the brain. All patients were treated with corticosteroids, and six were managed with additional immunotherapies. Finally, ten RP patients were improved and discharged. Conclusion neurological deficits vary widely in RP patients with CNS involvement, with cognitive decline as the most common feature. Inflammatory changes in the CSF indicate a neuroinflammatory mechanism involved in the pathogenesis of RP. Distinct imaging features on cranial MRI are closely associated with the involvement into CNS in RP, offering references for distinguishing the acute inflammation stage from the chronic degeneration stage during the development of RP.

title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots as Patient Information Tools: A Bilingual, Two-Round Evaluation of the e-Nabız Personal Health Record System
authors: Hossein Boustani Hezarani; Dilek Uslu
journal: Sağlık ve Sosyal Refah Araştırmaları Dergisi
abstract: This study evaluated four widely used large language models—ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek—as patient-information tools for e-Nabız, the national personal health record system of Türkiye, and tested whether their answers were reproducible one week apart. Thirty authentic patient questions spanning seven e-Nabız domains were submitted to each model in Turkish and English, in fresh sessions with default settings, and the protocol was repeated after one week (480 responses). A dated copy of the official e-Nabız User Guide served as the gold standard, and responses were scored blind for accuracy, completeness, the Global Quality Score, coverage, and safety, with readability computed using the Flesch, Flesch–Kincaid, Ateşman, and Bezirci–Yılmaz formulas. Model performance differed significantly in both languages, with Claude and Gemini outperforming ChatGPT and DeepSeek; two models performed better in Turkish. All models wrote above recommended reading levels, and although aggregate quality was stable between rounds, individual answers were substantially reworded and sometimes materially changed. Chatbots should complement, not replace, official e-Nabız guidance.

title: Extracellular vesicles in cardiovascular diseases: From molecular signatures to therapeutic applications
authors: Riya Nag; Syed Tasleem Raza; Wael Abdulrahman Almahmeed; Farzana Mahdi
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, emphasizing the need for sensitive biomarkers and effective therapeutic strategies. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound nanoparticles released by virtually all cell types that mediate intercellular communication through the transfer of proteins, lipids, messenger RNAs, microRNAs and DNA. Increasing evidence indicates that alterations in EV cargo contribute to the initiation and progression of multiple cardiovascular disorders, while also offering opportunities for minimally invasive diagnosis and targeted therapy. This review summarizes current evidence on the molecular mechanisms, diagnostic significance and therapeutic applications of EVs across major cardiovascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease and cardiomyopathies. Disease-specific EV-associated proteins and non-coding RNAs, particularly microRNAs, are discussed as candidate biomarkers for diagnosis, risk stratification, prognosis and treatment monitoring. The review also highlights emerging EV-based therapeutic approaches, including regenerative medicine, engineered EVs and targeted drug delivery systems, while critically discussing translational challenges such as EV heterogeneity, lack of standardized isolation and characterization protocols, scalability, regulatory considerations and the need for robust clinical validation. Most mechanistic and therapeutic evidence remains preclinical and EV biomarker assays are not yet established for routine care. In conclusion, EVs represent a promising platform for advancing precision cardiovascular medicine by integrating molecular diagnostics with innovative therapeutic strategies. Although substantial progress has been achieved, overcoming current technical, regulatory and clinical challenges through standardized methodologies and large-scale validation studies is essential for translating EV-based technologies into routine cardiovascular practice.

title: ROCK signaling at the interface of fibrosis and neurodegeneration: mechanisms and therapeutic potential
authors: Jeysson Sánchez-Suárez; Yvonne Adu-Rutledge; Kunho Bae; Hyungwoo Lee; Anton Lennikov; Nakyung Ryoo; Anil Upreti; Aruvi Vijikumar; William P. Miller; Leo A. Kim
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinases 1 and 2 (ROCK1 and ROCK2) regulate cytoskeletal dynamics, actomyosin contractility, extracellular matrix remodeling, and responses to mechanical stress. In the eye and central nervous system (CNS), these functions intersect with fibrocontractile scarring, neuronal dysfunction, impaired regeneration, and neuroinflammation. This review examines ROCK signaling at the interface of ocular fibrosis and neurodegeneration, emphasizing the retina as a setting in which neural injury and pathological remodeling can coexist. We outline the physiological and pathological consequences of ROCK-mediated mechanotransduction, using peripheral fibrosis only as brief comparative context, and examine its relationship with MRTF/SRF and YAP/TAZ transcriptional modules. We then assess evidence from ocular fibrotic disease, axonal regeneration, synaptic plasticity, microglial activation, and CNS injury-associated scarring, distinguishing direct ROCK-dependent mechanisms from extrapolation across tissues. ROCK1 and ROCK2 display overlapping functions with context-dependent specialization, but current evidence does not support a universal division of labor between the isoforms. Single-cell, spatial, and multi-omics approaches offer opportunities to identify disease-relevant cell populations, although transcript abundance alone cannot establish kinase activity or therapeutic dependence. Finally, we consider ocular and neural therapeutic development, including isoform-informed targeting, local delivery, and mechanism-aligned combinations. The central challenge is to suppress persistent pathological remodeling while preserving physiological repair and beneficial neural or glial responses. Resolving the cellular, spatial, and temporal requirements for ROCK signaling will be essential for testing whether antifibrotic and neuroprotective effects can be achieved together.

title: Efficacy and safety of low-power (20 W) catheter ablation for typical atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia: a prospective multicenter study
authors: Lae‐Young Jung; Chang Hee Kwon; In Geol Song; Ji Hyun Lee; Minsu Kim
abstract: Background Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) is the most common supraventricular tachycardia. Although catheter ablation is the definitive treatment, atrioventricular (AV) block requiring permanent pacemaker implantation remains a major safety concern. Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a low-power (20 W) slow pathway ablation strategy for typical AVNRT. Methods In this prospective multicenter study, 203 consecutive patients (mean age 54.4 ± 17.3 years; 59.6% women) underwent slow pathway ablation initiated at 20 W, with power escalation as needed. Variables associated with requiring higher power were analyzed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Results Initial success at 20 W was achieved in 170 patients (83.7%); 33 patients (16.3%) required higher power, with an overall acute success rate of 99.5%. Compared with patients who achieved success at 20 W, those requiring higher power were younger and had higher pre-ablation heart rates. On univariable analysis, younger age [odds ratio [OR] 0.66 per 10-year increase, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54–0.83; p < 0.001] and higher pre-ablation heart rate (OR 1.88 per 10-bpm increase, 95% CI 1.30–2.73; p < 0.001) were associated with the need for higher power. Transient AV block occurred in 1.9% of patients, and no cases of permanent AV block (0%, 95% CI 0%–1.8%) or pacemaker implantation were observed. During 18.3 ± 4.1 months of follow-up, recurrence occurred in two patients (0.9%). Conclusion An initial 20 W ablation strategy provides high efficacy with a favorable safety profile and no permanent AV block observed in this cohort. Younger age and a higher baseline heart rate predicted the need for power escalation, supporting an initial low-power approach for AVNRT ablation.

title: Efficacy and safety of exercise rehabilitation across the valve intervention pathway: A systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: ShanShan Lin; Haitao Wang; Ying Zhu; Dian Zhao; Tao Yu; Keli Huang; Xinlei He; Qin Jiang
abstract: Background The benefits and safety of exercise-based rehabilitation across the valve intervention pathway remain uncertain. We assessed its effects on exercise capacity, cardiac function, postoperative recovery, and reported adverse events. Methods We searched eight English and Chinese databases for randomised controlled trials of rehabilitation initiated before, around, or after surgical or transcatheter valve intervention. Outcomes were 6-min walk distance (6MWD), peak oxygen uptake (peak VO 2 ), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), postoperative length of stay, reported adverse events, and pulmonary complications. Principal analyses used random-effects models. We assessed outcome-specific risk of bias with RoB 2 and evidence certainty with GRADE, and performed subgroup interaction and sensitivity analyses. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261509016. Results Twenty-nine trials were included. Rehabilitation increased 6MWD (19 trials; mean difference [MD] 40.95 m, 95% CI 27.10 to 54.81), peak VO 2 [eight trials; standardised mean difference (SMD) 0.32, 0.07 to 0.57], and LVEF (14 trials; MD 4.41 percentage points, 2.26 to 6.56), and shortened postoperative hospital stay (16 trials; MD −1.77 days, −2.41 to −1.13). Reported adverse events were less frequent [14 estimable trials; risk ratio (RR) 0.53, 0.33 to 0.85], as were pulmonary complications (seven trials; RR 0.62, 0.50 to 0.77). Heterogeneity was substantial for 6MWD, LVEF, and hospital stay. Prediction intervals crossed the null for all outcomes except pulmonary complications. The peak VO 2 result was no longer statistically significant after excluding high-risk results. Evidence certainty was low for pulmonary complications and very low for the other outcomes. Conclusion Exercise-based rehabilitation may improve functional and postoperative outcomes around valve intervention, but the magnitude and applicability of benefits remain uncertain. Diverse event definitions prevent the pooled adverse-event result from establishing exercise-specific safety. Larger trials with standardised interventions, outcome assessment, and longer follow-up are needed.

title: Bone morphogenetic protein 12: a novel target for cardiovascular disease
authors: Stephania C. Isaza; Miguel Á. Hernández-García; Carlos Ernesto Fernández-García; Carolina Pérez-Utrera; María Álvarez‐Rubal; José M. Muñoz; Alfonsa Friera; Carmelo García‐Monzón; Almudena Gómez‐Hernández; Pedro Landete; Javier Egea; Fernándo Alfonso; Águeda González‐Rodríguez
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 12 (BMP12) is known to regulate mesenchymal differentiation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Given its structural and signaling similarities to BMP2, which promotes osteogenic phenotypic switching and pro-atherogenic responses in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), BMP12 may also contribute to vascular remodeling and atherosclerosis progression. This translational study aimed to unravel BMP12 involvement in cardiovascular disease (CVD). BMP12 effects on atherogenesis-related processes in VSMCs in absence or presence of BMP type I receptor inhibitors (DMH2 and LDN-193189) were evaluated. Additionally, circulating BMP12 levels were measured in a well-characterized cohort of patients with CV risk factors and correlated with cardiometabolic disorders and vascular damage markers. Results from the experimental study showed increased migration and calcification in BMP12-treated VSMCs. Mechanistically, BMP12 induced expression of osteogenic markers (RUNX2 and ALP) and genes related to cellular migration (Mmp9), while reducing contractile marker Desmin. These pro-atherogenic effects were blocked using BMP type I receptor inhibitors. Furthermore, the clinical study revealed higher serum BMP12 levels in patients with CVD and type 2 diabetes. Moreover, circulating BMP12 concentrations were elevated in patients with carotid and femoral plaques, correlating with plaque volume. Notably, BMP12 emerged as an independent predictor of femoral atherosclerosis. Collectively, these findings identify BMP12 as a previously unrecognized mediator of vascular remodeling, promoting pro-atherogenic effects in VSMCs through canonical BMP signaling. The association between elevated circulating BMP12 levels and subclinical vascular damage further supports its potential value as a contributor to atherosclerosis progression and as a promising novel candidate biomarker for CV risk.

title: Peripartum cardiomyopathy complicating major postpartum haemorrhage with pre-eclampsia and HELLP syndrome
authors: Ahmed Ali Kindawi; Shamma Al‐Inizi
journal: International Journal of Reproduction Contraception Obstetrics and Gynecology
abstract: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a rare, potentially life-threatening cause of heart failure, developing in the later stages of pregnancy, or immediately postpartum. Diagnosis can become challenging as obstetric emergencies may provide differing explanations for cardiovascular collapse. We demonstrate a rare case of acute severe biventricular failure occurring very soon after an emergency Caesarean section for a pregnancy complicated by HELLP syndrome in the setting of post-partum pre-eclampsia and severe postpartum haemorrhage. The diagnostic value of an urgent echocardiogram in an obstetric emergency is underlined and the challenges faced by clinicians in managing two serious medical emergencies at the same time are highlighted.

title: Efficient neuroanalytic local–global learning with dual-branch CNN–lightweight Swin Transformer for Alzheimer’s disease analysis
authors: Saddam Hussain Khan; Rashid Iqbal; Saeed Alqahtani; Rafi Us Shan; Abdulaziz Alhefdhi; Bader Fahad Alkhamees; Karim Gasmi; Arshad Ali
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is one of the main causes of dementia, where early detection is critical for postponing the progression of the disease and timely treatment. Recent computer-aided diagnosis using deep learning with structural MRI has shown optimal performance; however, the rising number of model parameters and high computational requirements make the deployment challenging in resource-limited environments. This study proposes an efficient deep learning framework named “NeuroCST” based on a dual-branch network architecture incorporating an enhanced EfficientNet-based CNN and a Lightweight Swin Transformer working independently to capture local and global information of AD. The enhanced Efficient Convolution branch extracts fine-grained morphological features using depthwise separable convolution and residual learning for texture capturing. Consequently, the customized SwinLite Transformer branch models global contextual dependencies using Efficient SwinLite Transformer blocks with attention, shifted-window partitioning, and MLP. These dual-branch diverse feature vectors are then concatenated and processed by a spatial attention mechanism, NeuroCST-SA, for optimal pixel selection to reduce redundancy and discriminate minor contrast and texture inter-class variation. The proposed NeuroCST is evaluated on the public Kaggle AD dataset, which contains 6,400 original and 33,984 augmented MRI images (40,384 in total) in four classes: Mild Demented, Moderate Demented, Non-Demented, and Very Mild Demented. The NeuroCST-SA performs better on diverse experimental setups, both augmented and original, than existing CNNs and ViTs, achieving 98.42% accuracy, 98.50% sensitivity, 98.60% precision, and an F1-score of 98.55% (mean, with a standard deviation of 2.49% across holdout cross-validation). The base NeuroCST model has 15.3 million parameters and 5.2 GFLOPs, and the NeuroCST-SA variant has 14.8 million parameters, 4.9 GFLOPs, and a processing time of 11.4 ms per image. The performance demonstrates the effective integration of CNN and transformer in capturing diverse local–global features for robust AD classification.

title: Cardiovascular Effects of Childhood Radiotherapy
authors: Alexandra Khorasanchi; Jenna Farris; Taylor Choi; William H. Frishman; Wilbert S. Aronow
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is an important, well-studied late effect of childhood cancer therapy that may manifest many years after treatment. Radiotherapy, particularly when the heart is exposed, has been associated with multiple cardiovascular complications, including heart failure, coronary artery disease, valvular disease, and arrhythmias. This review examines the cardiovascular effects of radiotherapy in childhood and adolescent cancer survivors, with a focus on the mechanisms of radiation-induced injury, major cardiovascular outcomes, factors influencing long-term risk, and advances in cardiac-sparing radiotherapy and surveillance. The literature indicates radiotherapy was associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiovascular disease. Cardiovascular risk was influenced by radiation dose and the volume and location of cardiac tissue exposed, as well as age at treatment, anthracycline exposure, and traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Modern radiation techniques, including intensity-modulated and proton therapy, have aimed to reduce cardiac exposure. However, long-term clinical outcome data for these approaches remain limited. These findings support long-term cardiovascular surveillance of childhood cancer survivors and emphasize the importance of minimizing cardiac radiation exposure and addressing modifiable cardiovascular risk factors. Improved assessment of radiation dose to specific cardiac structures may further enable individualized risk stratification and surveillance.

title: Impact of Documentation Aids on the Inclusion of Salient Left-Ventricular Late Gadolinium Enhancement Characteristics in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging Impressions
authors: Kailash Singh; Michelle Fang; Makiya Nakashima; Christopher Nguyen; W. H. Wilson Tang; Deborah H. Kwon; Po‐Hao Chen; David J. Chen
journal: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine
abstract: Abstract Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is a key diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM). However, the completeness of LGE reporting in routine CMR impressions remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to evaluate the impact of large language model (LLM)-assisted reporting on the consistency of LGE pattern, distribution, and severity documentation in CMR impressions for ICM and NICM. We analyzed 828 unstructured (1990–2023) and 400 structured (2024–2025) CMR reports to identify documentation of LGE pattern, distribution, and severity. A Llama 3 language model fine-tuned on 27,000 structured CMR reports was used to generate 9650 CMR impressions; LGE attributes were extracted using an LLM judge. LLM reporting behavior was further assessed using quantized low-rank adaptation adapters trained on structured and unstructured impressions. Structured reporting captured LGE pattern more frequently than unstructured reporting overall (85.5% vs. 61.0%, p = 9.60 × 10 −7 ) and for ICM (90.0% vs. 69.4%, p = 0.005). LLM-generated impressions demonstrated more frequent reporting of LGE distribution (75.3%) and severity (70.9%) versus structured and unstructured reports ( p < 0.001). Fine-tuning with an adapter trained on unstructured impressions significantly improved reporting of all three LGE attributes. Structured reporting improved LGE pattern documentation, but gaps in LGE distribution and severity documentation persisted across human report formats. LLM-generated impressions achieved broader attribute coverage for LGE distribution and severity. Fine-tuning on unstructured data improved model performance, suggesting that passive augmentation with data capturing the documentation styles of multiple providers may help to address reporting gaps.
